 Tennessee to require proof of citizenship for new vehicle registrations in 2027
 2026-11-18 20:02:34
 Dwayne Page
 Tennessee drivers will face a new requirement when registering a vehicle for the first time beginning in January.
 The DeKalb County Clerk’s Office is reminding motorists to bring proof of citizenship or lawful presence to avoid delays when registering their vehicles.
 County Clerk James L. (Jimmy) Poss said the new requirement, which takes effect January 1, 2027, stems from legislation passed by the Tennessee General Assembly earlier this year.
 Under Tennessee Code Annotated Section 55-4-144, anyone applying for an initial vehicle registration that includes issuing a license plate must provide documentation establishing U.S. citizenship, lawful permanent residency or federally authorized temporary presence in the country.
 Acceptable documentation includes a REAL ID-compliant license, Tennessee driver’s license or Tennessee photo identification card, along with other documents approved by the state.
 The requirement applies statewide and will be handled locally by county clerk offices.
 Annual vehicle registration renewals will not be affected by the new documentation requirement.
 The Tennessee Department of Revenue has published a list of acceptable documents and identification as follows
 Acceptable Documentation for Initial Vehicle Registrations 
 Effective January 1, 2027, Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-4-144 requires applicants seeking initial registrations for certain motor vehicles to provide documentation that the applicant is a U.S. citizen, a lawful permanent resident of the United States, or a person whose presence in the United States has been authorized by the federal government for a specific purpose and for a specified period of authorized stay.
 Documentation in either paper or electronic format is acceptable. Acceptable electronic formats include electronic images displayed on a cell phone or any other type of portable electronic device. All forms of proof must be unexpired.
 Acceptable License Types 
 The following license types are deemed satisfactory proof for purposes of initial registration:
 • REAL ID-compliant license
 • Tennessee driver license
 • Tennessee temporary driver license
 • Tennessee photo identification license
 • Tennessee temporary photo identification license
 Acceptable Documentation of U.S. Citizenship 
 • Official birth certificate issued by a U.S. state, jurisdiction or territory (Puerto Rico,
 U.S. Virgin Islands, Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, Swain’s Island, Guam)
 o Puerto Rico birth certificates issued prior to July 1, 2010, are invalid under Puerto Rico law and will not be accepted. Citizens of Puerto Rico born before July 1, 2010, should provide an updated, reissued certificate.
 • U.S. Certificate of Birth Abroad (DS-1350 or FS-545)
 • Report of Birth Abroad of a Citizen of the U.S. (FS-240)
 • Valid, unexpired U.S. Passport
 • Certificate of Citizenship (N560 or N561)
 • Certificate of Naturalization (N550, N570 or N578)
 • U.S. Citizen Identification Card (I-197, I-179)
 Acceptable Documentation of Lawful Permanent Resident Status 
 • Permanent Resident Alien Card (I-551)
 • Foreign passport stamped by the U.S. Government indicating that the holder has been “Processed for I-551”
 • Permanent Resident Re-entry Permit (I-327)
 • Arrival Departure Form I-94 with “Temporary I-551” stamp and holder’s photograph affixed
 • Travel Document issued to Refugees (I-571)
 • Form I-94 stamped with one of the following statuses: Asylee, Parolee or Parole, Refugee, Asylum, HP-humanitarian parolee or PIP-public interest parolee
 Acceptable Documentation of Temporary Legal Presence 
 • Conditional Resident Alien Card (I-551)
 • Valid Foreign Passport with Valid Visa and I-94 attached
 o Note: The passport must have an English translation
 • Valid Foreign Passport with I-94W attached
 o Holders of F1, F2, M1, or M2 status should also present a valid SEVIS I-20
 o Holders of J1 or J2 status should also present a valid DS-2019
